entries.reason: The unrestricted polynomial transformer can decide SAT first and emit a constant low-treewidth YES or NO formula. The exact statement is theorem-equivalent to P = NP and isolates no independent separator mechanism.
salvage: H009 restricts the transformer to local certified rewrites.
H100 additionally requires a decreasing local potential and forbids a global answer channel.

entries.reason: The unrestricted transformer can decide SAT and emit a one-bit submodular function encoding only the answer, so the exact formulation is circular rather than a submodular mechanism.
salvage: H043 restricts the lift grammar to local submodular constructions.

entries.reason: After deciding SAT, the transformer can emit a constant feasible or infeasible totally-unimodular system. The statement does not constrain where the semantic work occurs.
salvage: H044 fixes a local totally-unimodular lift grammar and explicit accounting.

entries.reason: An unrestricted transformer can decide SAT before emitting a constant-size feasible or infeasible moment instance. The constant relaxation level therefore does not define an independent algorithmic route.
salvage: H045 restricts the SoS lift to a finite local grammar.
H071 attacks that restricted route through theta-rank stability.

entries.reason: The interface-DAG node language, original-variable support, denotation size, and composition semantics are not fixed. A single boundary symbol may hide a globally hard residual function, so the claimed node and boundary bounds are not falsifiable resources.
salvage: H102 fixes a typed circuit language and charges complete original-variable support.

entries.reason: The arbitrary polynomial-time compiler can decide SAT first and choose between two fixed graphs with the desired alpha/theta behavior. The statement is target-equivalent to P = NP and does not isolate a theta mechanism.
salvage: H094 retains the valid one-sided dual certificate lemma.
H103 restricts the compiler to a fixed one-pass local signed-incidence transduction.
